claims.exact_statement: For every Boolean g with mean mu and every integer r>=1, p=2^-r, the genuine Boolean activation F=1+A_r(g-1) satisfies E F=1-p+p mu, Pr(F=-1)=p(1-mu)/2, I(F)=p[I(g)+r(1-mu)], and H(F)=p[H(g)-phi(mu^2)]+2rp(1-mu^2)+(2^r-1)phi(p^2(1-mu)^2)+phi((1-p+p mu)^2). Data influences are p I_i(g) and each control influence is p(1-mu). If g is nonconstant and has full Walsh support, F has full Walsh support.
refutes: The balanced-core activation formula may be applied unchanged to arbitrary-mean seeds.
scope_exclusions: Does not preserve all-coordinate restriction criticality.

claims.exact_statement: For every nonconstant Boolean seed g and every epsilon>0 there is a genuine Boolean F with full Walsh support, I(F)<=epsilon, max_i I_i(F)/I(F)<=epsilon, Pr(F=-1)<=epsilon, and |H(F)/I(F)-H(g)/I(g)|<=epsilon. More precisely, for every eta>0 the supremum of H(F)/I(F) over nonconstant full-support F satisfying I(F)<=eta, max_i I_i(F)/I(F)<=eta, and Pr(F=-1)<=eta equals C_FEI in the extended-real sense.
contributors: prior tensor-activation and full-support sources as credited

proof_dependencies.role: odd-negative-count full-support surgery and entropy continuity

refutes: Full Walsh support plus small total influence, diffuse coordinate influences, and rare output define an FEI-easier universal class.
scope_exclusions: The embedded functions are not balanced.
Cheap controls mean restriction-step criticality is not preserved.
No numerical FEI constant is obtained.
